newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up, focus on finance stocks.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up, focus on finance stocks.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended up on Friday on the back of active buying of finance counters, brokers said.
Brokers said the encouraging debut of Unibank and strong first quarter net profit of finance company Putra Surya Multi Finance PSMD helped boost sentiment on the sector.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.03 points, or 0.44 percent, to 695.02 points after hitting an intra-day high of 696.15 points.
Gainers led losers by 71 to 48, with 69 counters unchanged.
Total turn-over was estimated at 433.2 billion rupiah, compared with 460 billion rupiah on Thursday.
Analysts and brokers expected the market to move in a narrow-range on Monday as many companies had announced their first quarter results.
"First quarter results of some of the most-eagerly awaited companies have been announced. There is not much news to drive buying in blue chips," an analyst with a European securities firm said.
But he said President Suharto's minor cabinet shuffle on Friday might lead investors to speculate further in the coming week on the successsion.
Suharto replaced Information Minister Harmoko with retiring army chief of staff General Hartono. Harmoko was named minister for special affairs and is expected to take over as speaker of parliament.
Brokers and analysts said the move was surprising but did not have any impact on overall market sentiment.
Banking stocks such as Bank Negara Indonesia, Unibank and Ficorinvest were among active stocks.
BNI topped the active list as it fell 25 rupiah to 1,625 rupiah, with some 25 million shares traded due to profit-taking, brokers said.
Unibank made a strong debut, closing at 900 rupiah against an offer price of 675 rupiah after touching a high of 975 rupiah with some 19 million shares traded.
Ficorinvest was active on renewed market talk that the central bank was likely to sell its stake in the company.
Locally-led buying was seen in shoe-maker Kasogi International after its recent announcement that it intended to join forces with a foreign partner, brokers said.
